Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (consistent with transcript and DDx): Dermatitis/eczema of the hands, most likely irritant contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure to cleaning products with inconsistent glove use.

- Relevant differential diagnoses and reasoning (aligned with transcript data):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis (High): Strongly supported by palm-dominant involvement, itching, cracking, exposure to cleaners, and glove-use pattern.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis (Medium-High): Possible given exposure to cleaning agents; could be an sensitization issue; patch testing could help identify specific allergens.
  - Hand dermatitis/eczema (Medium): Fits chronic dry, itchy hands with fissures; may reflect overall eczema phenotype exacerbated by irritants/allergens.
  - Xerosis related to diabetes/metabolic dryness (Medium-Low): Diabetes can contribute to dry skin; focal palmar cracking is more consistent with contact dermatitis given exposure.
  - Traumatic/irritant friction dermatitis (Supplementary): Mechanical irritation from repetitive cleaning tasks could contribute to fissuring.

- Working diagnosis and management priorities: 
  - Primary: Irritant contact dermatitis of the hands.
  - Secondary considerations: Allergic contact dermatitis; hand dermatitis/eczema; xerosis contributing to symptoms.

- Plan summary (key decisions):
  - Trigger/exposure reduction: Strongly emphasize wearing gloves during cleaning at all times.
  - Pharmacologic therapy: Use topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation; apply a stronger emollient several times daily (3–4 times) for the next 2 weeks.
  - Follow-up: Reassess in 1–2 weeks; return sooner if spreading or worsening; consider additional therapies if not improved after 10–14 days.
  - Access to care: Prescription to be sent to pharmacy.

Management Plan

- Implement protective measures: Wear gloves during cleaning at all times; minimize exposure to cleaning products.
- Medications:
  - Topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (name not specified) – use as directed; duration not specified in transcript.
  - Emollient cream (stronger moisturizer) – coat on the hands 3–4 times daily for 2 weeks.
  - Antihistamine previously tried (dose/route/frequency not documented) – not currently active in plan; note prior use without relief.
- Monitoring and follow-up: Return in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen or spread; if no improvement after 10–14 days, reevaluate and discuss additional treatment options.
- Patient education: Education on glove use and skin care; prescription provided to the patient’s pharmacy.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Irritant contact dermatitis — High
  - Justification: Occupational exposure to cleaning products with inconsistent glove use; palmar involvement with cracking and itching; chronic course consistent with irritant dermatitis.
- Allergic contact dermatitis — Medium-High
  - Justification: Possible sensitization to cleaning agents; pruritus and fissuring fit dermatitis spectrum; patch testing could identify specific allergens.
- Hand dermatitis/eczema — Medium
  - Justification: Chronic hand dryness and itching with fissures; may be exacerbated by irritants/allergens; can respond to steroids and moisturizers.
- Xerosis with diabetes-related dryness — Medium-Low
  - Justification: Diabetes can predispose to dry skin (legs also dry); palmar focal cracking remains more typical of dermatitis due to exposures.
